concept_reviews.independent_relation: Translation taking O to O_1 takes OA and OB to rays with the same respective directions at O_1, preserving the convex angle. Actual fig-229 shows paired up-right and down-right directions.
The direction angle is the common-origin convex magnitude, independent of chosen origin. A direction with itself has magnitude 0 degrees; opposite directions give the straight magnitude 180 degrees.
Two convex angles with corresponding sides in the same directions are congruent. Supporting-line parallelism alone is insufficient to specify same versus opposite ray directions.
The angle between directions denotes a magnitude and chooses the convex rather than reflex sector formed by the common-origin rays.

derived_relation_reviews.solution: Same quarter-turn senses preserve theta; differing perpendicular-ray choices give 180 - theta. Both acute or both obtuse excludes the latter.

Translation and a half-turn establish equal convex magnitudes. The construction works regardless of the location case and allows parallel or coincident supporting lines.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A=0, B=b, C=c along their common line with 0<b<c. AB and BC both point positive, whereas CB points negative. The angle between ray directions ignores their differing origins.

Draw the given rays AB and CD. Set u=B-A and v=D-C; at the prescribed M draw rays MX and MY toward X=M+u and Y=M+v. Their convex angle equals the magnitude between the AB and CD directions by common-origin translation. Supporting lines through M may coincide with existing supports. No numeric magnitude is specified.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Translate the first vertex to the second, preserving both side directions; apply a half-turn about the second vertex. It reverses both sides and maps the first convex angle to the second. Both transformations are isometries, so the angles are congruent. At a common vertex the relevant sectors are vertical angles, not a linear pair.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Translate to one vertex. The same-direction pair becomes one common ray; the other corresponding pair consists of opposite rays. source_reviews.independent_solution: Let theta be the first convex magnitude, J a quarter-turn, and u,v its side directions. Corresponding perpendicular directions are s1*Ju and s2*Jv with independent signs. Equal signs preserve theta under a common quarter-turn; unequal signs yield 180-theta by one reversal. Same-type angles exclude the supplementary alternative. Swapping side correspondence does not change the unoriented magnitude.
